positive_controls.argument: The explicit beneficiary, horizon and nontradeable constraints identify which feedback could change the valued decision.
The outcome and constraint definition selects which integrated behaviors are relevant and exposes omitted affected parties.
The named outcome and constraints make lost benefit and transferred harm explicit when ordering consequential uncertainty.
The outcome and nonnegotiable constraints distinguish a justified change of means from unacknowledged loss of purpose.
The explicit outcome, affected population and constraints supply the substantive target and harm boundaries for the trial.
Named outcomes, horizon and nontradeable constraints provide substantive needs and rationale for the authoritative intent state.
Explicit beneficiary and outcome framing identifies the consequential value assumption whose uncertainty must remain visible.
Outcome and constraint framing selects the behavior or feasibility question that would matter to the beneficiary decision.
The named beneficiary, desired outcome and constraints define substantive intended-use questions and expose unrepresented interests.
Outcome and constraint framing informs substantive acceptance criteria and residual beneficiary obligations before the decision.
Explicit nontradeable safety and externality constraints identify affected persons and consequential losses for hazard inquiry.
The explicit beneficiary, use horizon and constraints sharpen the top claim and reveal benefit assumptions needing separate support.
Outcome and affected-party framing makes the anomaly consequence and intended correction objective explicit for disposition.
The beneficiary outcome, constraints and abandonment conditions supply substantive go, redirect and stop considerations.
The explicit outcome horizon and constraints distinguish the desired target from the quantity that the forecast can actually predict.
The value model identifies affected interests and nontradeable constraints for the residual-risk judgment.
The explicit constraints and affected parties supply consequential harm dimensions that a reversibility-only control choice could miss.
